issue_context.title: Wrong strategic ThreeWayMergePatch because of "creationTimestamp":null
issue_context.body:
#### What happened:
Calling `strategicpatch.CreateThreeWayMergePatch` results in `{"metadata":{"creationTimestamp":null}}`, but expected `{}` instead.

code example:
```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/schema"
	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch"
	k8sscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
)

func main() {
	scheme := k8sscheme.Scheme

	originalData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
	targetData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":null},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
	currentData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)

	gvk := schema.GroupVersionKind{
		Group:   "",
		Version: "v1",
		Kind:    "Namespace",
	}

	versionedObject, _ := scheme.New(gvk)
	lookupPatchMeta, _ := strategicpatch.NewPatchMetaFromStruct(versionedObject)
	patch, _ := strategicpatch.CreateThreeWayMergePatch(originalData, targetData, currentData, lookupPatchMeta, true)

	fmt.Printf("%s\n", patch) // OUTPUT: {"metadata":{"creationTimestamp":null}}
}
```

This is caused by a wrong encoding of `metav1.ObjectMeta{}`:
```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
)

func main() {
	originalData, err := json.Marshal(metav1.ObjectMeta{})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("error: %v\n", err)
	}

	fmt.Printf("%s\n", originalData) // OUTPUT: {"creationTimestamp":null}
}
```

#### Environment:
```
k8s.io/api v0.22.1
k8s.io/apimachinery v0.22.1
k8s.io/client-go v0.22.1
```

I've created a pull request.
Marshal of empty ObjectMeta do have null creationTimestamp field.
But I think ThreeWayMergePatch behaves correctly. In your case:
```go
originalData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
targetData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":null},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
currentData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
```
originalData is the same with currentData. And the delta change of targetData is from `"creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"` to `"creationTimestamp":null`. Apply ThreeWayMergePatch, and we get patch `{"metadata":{"creationTimestamp":null}}`. This is correct. If we get `{}`, then nothing will change.

After my change, I make some tests and get the output listed below.
```diff
originalData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
-targetData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":null},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
+targetData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)
currentData := []byte(`{"kind":"Namespace","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{"name":"namespace","creationTimestamp":"2021-09-06T20:09:23Z"},"spec":{},"status":{}}`)

fmt.Printf("%s\n", patch) // OUTPUT: {"metadata":{"creationTimestamp":null}}
```
@liggitt @sttts I'm sure we've talked about it in the past but I can't remember, what are your thoughts? i.e. #104857 creates a custom marshaller

I don't have all the strategic merge patch context paged in, but the custom MarshalJSON implementation won't work (see comment at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104857/files#r706719139)

review_comments: This will break encoding of all objects that inline objectmeta (which is all API objects) since it hijacks the MarshalJSON implementation of the containing object
Indeed, the MarshalJSON function is promoted to the embedder. We will have to find another solution instead.
It's my blunder. I didn't think thoroughly. As for Marshaller, I can only come up with specific Marshaller for each resource type, which is kind of cumbersome. Is there any suggestion?
not really... I spent a while trying to figure out a solution in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/67610 and couldn't come up with anything reasonable
Maybe a bit too drastic, but what about creating a json fork / wrapper library that implements https://github.com/golang/go/issues/11939?
